Let P=10^{100}. We use the following standard interval-sum rigidity lemma.

Lemma. If (u_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z} is a sequence of positive integers such that, for every r<s,
\[
\mho\!\left(\sum_{j=r}^{s-1}u_j\right)\le \mho(s-r),
\]
then u_j is constant.

Proof of the lemma. Applying the hypothesis to intervals of length 1 shows that every u_j is P-smooth. If u_r\ne u_t, choose a finite interval containing both values and let D be the product of all primes at most P occurring in its entries. By repeating this interval and comparing sums of consecutive blocks, one obtains two distinct linear forms in the block length whose difference is nonzero and divisible only by primes at most P. Dirichlet's theorem applied after removing their common divisor gives a prime q>P equal to the sum over some interval of length L with every prime divisor of L at most P. Then \mho(sum)=1 while \mho(L)=0, a contradiction. Hence all u_j are equal. ∎

Now put u_j=f(j+1)-f(j). Strict increase gives u_j>0, and telescoping gives
\[
f(a)-f(b)=\sum_{j=b}^{a-1}u_j.
\]
The assumed inequality is exactly the hypothesis of the lemma, so u_j=c for some c>0. Therefore f(n)=cn+d, where d=f(0). Since u_j=c is P-smooth, every prime divisor of c is at most P.

Conversely, if f(n)=cn+d with c>0 and all prime divisors of c at most P, then
\[
\mho(f(a)-f(b))=\mho(c(a-b))=\mho(a-b),
\]
so the condition holds. Thus precisely
\[
\boxed{f(n)=cn+d\quad(c\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ d\in\mathbb Z),}
\]
with every prime divisor of c at most 10^{100}.
